text:
maria: Quick sketch + question — proposing we collapse the left index into three primary headings (Project, Model hub, Observability) and surface other items in contextual flyouts to reduce visual clutter. Also thinking about making deep links canonical so external links are stable. Thoughts?

sam: Sounds promising. main worry: breadcrumb stability when items are hidden. folks expect a copy/pasteable stable path.

lina: Agree. Breadcrumbs should always show the logical path (Org > Project X > Model > Versions) even if sidebar label is compacted. That keeps automation/scripts intact.

alex: +1 on canonical paths. Current mix of hash routes and full paths is messy. Propose we standardize on full path URLs (no hash routing) and reserve hash for ephemeral UI state only.

maria: Example canonical urls I mocked: `https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/redwood/projects/rosetta/models/rosetta-7b?panel=metrics` and ephemeral UI state like `#breadcrumbs=compact`.

ethan: A11y note: when groups collapse, keyboard focus order must follow the breadcrumb/heading, not the visual collapsed group. Also ensure the live region announces when focus lands in a flyout panel so screen readers know where they are.

sam: UX question — when a user clicks a subitem inside a collapsed group, do we expand and navigate or navigate while keeping groups collapsed? which preserves context better?

lina: Navigate directly (keep groups collapsed) to save vertical space. But animate or briefly highlight which group contains the target (tiny toast: "Found under Model hub") and use `aria-live=polite` for announcement.

alex: For deep links from docs/emails we must support legacy hash routes for a migration window (suggest 6 months). Implement middleware that maps legacy hash patterns to canonical paths.

maria: How expensive will maintaining that mapping be?

ethan: Straightforward for now. Log unmatched legacy routes for 30 days and prune. Add telemetry flag `legacy_route_handled=true` when shim fires so we can monitor failures.

prod-bot: deploy-preview created: https://deploy-preview.redwood.ai/compact-left-index at `preview/compact-left-index` — includes routing shim + breadcrumb behavior tests.

sam: I'll run an accessibility sweep on the preview tomorrow. Quick checklist: 1) focus order 2) screenreader announcements for flyouts 3) link text clarity (avoid "click here") 4) keyboard expand/collapse with Enter/Space.

lina: Copy nit: instead of "Models" label maybe "Model hub" — reads better when compact. Also ensure breadcrumbs use full resource titles, not UI labels, so breadcrumbs are stable for automation.

maria: Love "Model hub". We'll try it in the preview. One more question: should bookmarks include panel state (e.g., which side panel was open)? pros: reproducible; cons: brittle with UI changes.

alex: Prefer minimal bookmarks: canonical path + stable query keys (e.g., `?eval=123`). Avoid serializing ephemeral panel states. Document supported query params so integrations can link reliably.

sam: Accessibility nit — when we canonicalize/redirect routes programmatically, call `focus()` on the main h1 and set `document.title` correctly so screen reader users aren’t lost.

maria: Great. Next steps: 1) ship preview to design + a11y 2) sam to run a11y sweep 3) eng to add legacy route telemetry 4) product to finalise query param contract. I'll post updated mocks and a screenshot shortly. :sparkles:

ethan: I'll prototype aria-live messages for the flyout and toast.

alex: I'll draft the route migration doc (mapping table + deprecation timeline) and share in this thread.

prod-bot: preview build passed e2e checks (3/3).
